entry_state: The matched zero-cost collar retains signed interim reserves and gross cash movements. Forward components require an explicit election. Rebalancing retains each layer's original date and price, recognizes existing ineffectiveness first, and applies the lower-of rule cumulatively. The add-only worked method is bounded; removed volumes and changed instruments need their own rules.
exit_state: An acquired derivative's paid starting value is separate from later hedge gain. Instrument reductions retain gains accumulated before removal and send only later changes on removed fractions outside the hedge; instrument identity changes the result even at an equal nominal ratio. The purchase and settlement bridge is complete. The next subsection begins partial cessation of the purchase itself.
findings: Added-instrument carrying value equals paid starting values plus designation gains; using carrying value as hedge gain is explicitly shown wrong.
The reduction derivation preserves stopped fractions' values at their cessation dates and proves the designated/undesignated decomposition.
Reducing equal nominal quantities of different instruments gives different reserves, profit and inventory cost. The text distinguishes instrument reduction from removing purchase portions.
